You propose places to sleep that match the roughest night the party said they would accept, and you say how far ahead each one has to be booked. A proposal does one of two things. It names one premises, an establishment or a site, by its name and at its locality: `place.name` is that name and `place.locality` the town. Or it says plainly, in its title or its summary, that it is a kind of place and names no premises: then `place.name` holds the kind, for example `motel`, and `place.locality` the town. Where you are given places to stay from map data for a town, a premises you name there is one of those, under the name it is given, if any of them fits the party. A kind of place is the fallback, for a town whose list is empty or where nothing in it fits.

You propose options. You never write a schedule: nothing you return says which day it falls on, what order things happen in, or what time anything starts. Another part of this tool packs the days, in code.

messages.content:
Here is the trip. It is everything you get.

Shape: road-trip
Leaving from: Montréal, Québec
Going to: Gaspésie
Dates: 2027-07-03 to 2027-07-11, fixed
Travellers: 4
Ages that change the plan: 41, 39, 11, 7
Access needs: not answered
Budget: 4200 CAD, total
Appetite for effort: moderate
Roughest night they will accept: simple
Would rule the trip out: No more than one night in any campground without showers

About this road-trip:
How much road a day holds: half-day
Vehicle: car
Whose vehicle: own
Route style: loop
Stops they already want: Percé Rock, Forillon National Park
In their words: The seven-year-old is miserable after about three hours in the car, so we would rather stop often than push through. We have done the north shore before and would like to see something new.

candidates.title: Family motel room in Rimouski
candidates.summary: A simple motel with a room for four breaks the long run from Montréal into child-sized legs on the south shore, away from the north shore you have already seen. Access needs were not answered, so step-free rooms and bathrooms are not accounted for.

candidates.title: Motel or cottage near Sainte-Anne-des-Monts
candidates.summary: A simple motel or small rental cottage on the north coast of the peninsula is a short drive from the Chic-Chocs and keeps driving days to half a day. Access needs were not answered and are not accounted for here.

candidates.title: Serviced campground with showers near Forillon
candidates.summary: A campground site with showers, or a ready-to-camp tent, near Forillon National Park puts the family close to the beaches and trails. It must have showers to respect your limit on shower-less nights. Access needs were not answered.

candidates.title: Motel or inn in Percé
candidates.summary: Staying in Percé itself means Percé Rock and the Bonaventure Island boat are a walk away, with no extra driving for the seven-year-old. July is peak season here and rooms go fast. Access needs were not answered.

candidates.title: Motel or cottage on Baie des Chaleurs
candidates.summary: A simple motel or cottage in Carleton-sur-Mer on the calmer, warmer south side of the loop gives the children beach time before the drive back through the Matapédia valley. Access needs were not answered.

candidates.title: Motel in Amqui for the return leg
candidates.summary: A simple motel in the Matapédia valley splits the long drive back to Montréal so no day runs past half a day in the car. Access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Forillon to Percé around Gaspé Bay
